knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes a confidence interval for an unknown parameter from a random sample?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Parameter CIs target a parameter with coverage. They are not prediction intervals for the next observation, and not identical to hypothesis tests.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Sample-based interval for an unknown parameter with stated coverage.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reading a CI as a prediction claim or as a hypothesis test.

choices.label: A CI uses sample information to construct an interval for an unknown parameter under stated assumptions, with a frequentist coverage reading for that parameter.
A CI is a probability statement that the next observation falls inside the numerical interval.
A CI is the same decision procedure as a hypothesis test: both only accept or reject a null.
After seeing the data, a 95% CI means the parameter equals the interval midpoint with probability 95%.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A 95% CI for mean claim size μ is (80, 100). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Coverage reading; refuse prediction and HT conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Coverage is about μ and the procedure. Prediction readings and 'midpoint probability' misstate frequentist CIs; HT is a related but distinct task.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: 95% coverage for μ; refuse prediction reading and CI=HT collapse.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reading the CI as a probability for the next claim, or equating CIs with hypothesis tests.

choices.label: The interval comes from a procedure with 95% coverage for the unknown parameter μ under repeated sampling. It is not a 95% probability that the next claim falls in (80, 100), and it is not the same object as a hypothesis test.
There is a 95% chance the next claim falls in (80, 100).
The interval is a hypothesis test that automatically rejects every null outside (80, 100) without further structure.
μ equals 90 with probability 95%, because 90 is the midpoint.

worked_example.title: 95% z-interval for mean premium
worked_example.problem_statement: A random sample of n = 100 household premiums has x̄ = £450. Model premiums as Normal with known σ = £50. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean premium μ.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Write x̄ ± 1.96 σ/√n with √100 = 10.

steps.label: Standard error
steps.explanation: SE of the sample mean with known σ is σ/√n.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Using 1.96 × 50 = 98 as the half-width (forgetting /√n), which yields the nonsensical interval (352, 548) for a mean of 450 with n = 100.
